answer: Require each agent to earn a scarce, nontransferable reputation credential by completing randomly assigned tasks that are checked against independent evidence, with a kernel of trusted evaluators rotating across tasks. One person can still create many identities, but each must build its own verified history; copying a credential or coordinating identical submissions fails cross-checks. Like an island that admits newcomers only after demonstrated work, this raises the attacker’s cost to time, compute, and repeated exposure, rather than pretending identity is impossible to fake at dawn.
